title: Numerals 1: один Agrees Like an Adjective
description: The number 1 (один/одна/одно/одни) changes to match the gender of its noun, and the noun stays in its plain dictionary form: один стол, одна книга, одно окно.
descriptionRussian: Число 1 (один/одна/одно/одни) меняется по роду существительного, а само существительное остаётся в обычной словарной форме: один стол, одна книга, одно окно.
intro: The A1 numbers book taught you which form a noun takes after each number. This one goes further: what happens when the number phrase itself has to go into a case, and what the awkward numbers do. Starting with the one that behaves least like a number. It agrees with its noun like an adjective and leaves the noun alone, which nothing else here does.
rules: The number 1 is один and behaves like an adjective: it changes its ending to match the gender of its noun, and the noun stays in its plain dictionary form.
Masculine: один (один стол). Feminine: одна (одна книга). Neuter: одно (одно окно). Plural-only nouns: одни (одни часы).
Unlike the numbers 2 and up, один does NOT put the noun into the genitive. Один стол is plain nominative singular, not один стола.
Because один is adjective-type, when the whole phrase changes case, один and the noun decline together: об одной книге, с одним другом, к одному дому.
Choose the gender form from the noun's gender, not from English. In English 'one' never changes, but один must.
examples: У меня есть один брат. (I have one brother.) брат is masculine, so один; брат stays in its dictionary form.
На столе одна книга. (There is one book on the table.) книга is feminine, so одна; книга is plain nominative.
В комнате одно окно. (There is one window in the room.) окно is neuter, so одно.
Это одни часы. (This is one clock.) часы is a plural-only noun, so одни.
Я думаю об одной книге. (I am thinking about one book.) the phrase is prepositional: одна becomes одной, книга becomes книге.
Он пришёл с одним другом. (He came with one friend.) instrumental: один becomes одним, друг becomes другом.

items.hint: Брат is masculine. Which form of 'one' matches it?
items.explanation: Брат is a masculine noun, so 'one' takes the masculine form один. The noun stays in its plain dictionary form: один брат, not один брата. Одна is feminine, одно is neuter, and одни is for plural-only nouns.

items.promptEnglish: There is one book on the table.
items.hint: Книга is feminine. Match the gender.
items.explanation: Книга is feminine, so 'one' becomes одна. Like an adjective (новая книга), один agrees with the gender of its noun: одна книга. Один is masculine, одно is neuter, одни is for plural-only nouns.

items.promptEnglish: There is one window in the room.
items.hint: Окно is neuter. Which form of 'one' is neuter?
items.explanation: Окно is a neuter noun (it ends in -о), so 'one' takes the neuter form одно: одно окно. The noun does not change. Один is masculine, одна is feminine, одни is for plural-only nouns.

items.promptEnglish: I have already been waiting one minute.
items.hint: Минута is feminine, and 'for one minute' is the accusative of duration. Decline одна.
items.explanation: Минута is feminine, so 'one' is одна. Here the phrase is in the accusative (duration: 'for one minute'), and одна becomes одну, минута becomes минуту. Один declines with the noun, like an adjective. Один is masculine nominative, одно is neuter, одни is plural-only.

items.hint: С takes the instrumental. What is один in the instrumental?
items.explanation: The preposition с takes the instrumental, so the whole phrase declines: друг becomes другом, and один becomes одним. Один changes its ending just like an adjective in the instrumental (с новым другом). Одной is feminine, одного is genitive/animate accusative, один is the plain nominative.

items.promptEnglish: This is one clock, not two.
items.hint: Часы is a plural-only noun. Which form of 'one' goes with plural-only nouns?
items.explanation: Часы (clock/watch) exists only in the plural, so 'one' must take the plural form одни: одни часы. The same happens with очки (glasses): одни очки. Один, одна, and одно are all singular forms and cannot pair with a plural-only noun.

blanks: В письме было только _____ слово. (There was only one word in the letter.)
fillInBlank.grammarFocus: Слово is neuter (it ends in -о), so 'one' takes the neuter form одно: одно слово. Один agrees with the gender of its noun, like an adjective.

errorCorrection.explanation: Because один is adjective-type, it declines together with its noun when the phrase changes case. С takes the instrumental, so подруга becomes подругой and the feminine 'one' must become одной: с одной подругой. Одну is the accusative and одним the masculine instrumental.

errorCorrection.translationEnglish: There is only one student in the class.
errorCorrection.explanation: Unlike 2, 3, 4 and 5 and up, the number один does NOT push the noun into the genitive. The noun stays in its plain nominative singular: один студент. Студента is the genitive singular, the form you would use after два (два студента) but never after один. The rule of thumb: 1 leaves the noun alone, and only 2 and up reshape it.

errorCorrection.sentence: Я знаю только один студента здесь.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: I know only one student here.
errorCorrection.explanation: Студент is masculine ANIMATE, and with an animate noun the accusative of один borrows the genitive form: знаю одного студента. The bare один is the nominative / inanimate accusative.

minimalPairs.contextEnglish: There is one magazine on the shelf.
minimalPairs.explanation: Журнал is masculine, so 'one' is один, not одна. Один agrees with the gender of its noun just like an adjective. Choosing одна would be like saying 'новая журнал'.

Минута is feminine, so 'one' is одна, and here the phrase is in the accusative (the object of дайте), where одна becomes одну: одну минуту. Один (masculine nominative) does not match either the gender or the case.

reviewVocab.definition: the number 1; it behaves like an adjective and changes by gender (masculine один, feminine одна, neuter одно, plural-only одни). The noun stays in its plain form.
reviewVocab.example: Один стол, одна книга, одно окно, одни часы.

reviewVocab.definition: agreement by gender: matching the form of один (and adjectives) to the gender of the noun.
reviewVocab.example: Книга — женский род, поэтому одна книга.

reviewVocab.definition: with nouns that exist only in the plural (часы, очки, ножницы) the number 1 is одни.
reviewVocab.example: У меня одни очки и одни часы.

hints: кем? чем? - один declines like an adjective in the instrumental (compare новым)
о ком? о чём? - the prepositional of один, used after о / об
